Subject: FCCPS AI Advisory Committee – Follow‑Up, Assignments, and Next Steps

Dear Committee Members,

Thank you all for the thoughtful work and discussion at Meeting 6. I’m still compiling the full minutes (including the transcript) and will post them shortly, but I want to get key decisions and action items to you now.

We agreed to:
- Shift from an anthology of individually attributed pieces to **integrated policy sections** written in a **single committee voice**.
- Focus our condensation effort on the **WS‑POL policy sections** (A–O), while treating the workstream sections primarily as **appendix/supporting material**.
- Assign a **“head honcho”** to each WS‑POL section to integrate all contributions into concise, board‑readable policy language.
- **Extend our next meeting** (Thursday, April 24) to a 3‑hour working session (approx. 8:30–11:30) for live refining and alignment.

Over the next two weeks, I will:
- Maintain and update the **master document**, applying consistent formatting, headings, and citation style.
- **Clean up the Table of Contents** so it reflects the 17 WS‑POL sections rather than every preface and individual contribution.
- Review and revise **section prefaces** for neutrality and accuracy, especially where there may be AI‑generated/legacy phrasing that overstates disagreement.
- **Integrate head honcho drafts** into the master document and normalize style and structure.
- Draft a **10‑minute overview** for the School Board’s April 28 meeting and circulate it to you for review before I present.

---

Please note the deliverables and dates in bold:

1. **Review for Accuracy and Mischaracterization**  
   - As you are able, re‑read the current prefaces and summaries in your areas.  
   - **If you see a disagreement described that doesn’t match the actual written record, or if your position is misstated, contact me and/or the relevant head honcho by _Monday, April 14_.**

2. **Collaborate with Head Honchos**  
   - If you contributed to a section, you should:
     - Review that section’s condensed draft when the head honcho shares it.
     - Request inclusion of **critical missing points** or propose small wording tweaks.  
   - **Please send any must‑have edits or suggested insertions directly to the head honcho by _Wednesday, April 16_**, so they can refine before our extended April 24 meeting.

3. **Style and Length Guidance**  
   - Write in **committee voice** (e.g., “The committee recommends…”, “The committee believes…”), not individual “I” voice.
   - Use **plain language** oriented to lay board members.
   - For most WS‑POL sections, aim for **½–2 pages** per section in the final integrated draft (student‑use sections will likely be longer).

4. **Prepare for Extended Meeting (April 24)**  
   - Please **block 8:30–11:30 AM on Thursday, April 24** for our extended working session.  
   - Plan to bring a laptop and be ready to edit in the shared Google Doc during the meeting.

---

Each WS‑POL section has a designated head honcho responsible for **condensing and integrating** all existing contributions into a single, coherent section.

**Assignments**:

- **WS-POL-A – Guiding Principles, Motivation:** Thomas Colvin  
- **WS-POL-B – Adoption vs. Restriction Posture:** John Black  
- **WS-POL-C – Scope, Triaging, and Policy Crosswalk:** Adriana Palacios  
- **WS-POL-D – Definitions:** Jillian Burkley  
- **WS-POL-E – Staff and Teacher Use of AI:** Susan Nelson

- **WS-POL-F – Student Use – PreK–5:**  
- **WS-POL-G – Student Use – Grades 6–12:**  
  - **Consolidated under:** Elizabeth Chua  
  - These two student‑use sections (**F + G together**) will be combined and are expected to run **longer than 2 pages** due to complexity.

- **WS-POL-H – Student Use Categories, Controls, and Interaction Boundaries:**  
- **WS-POL-I – Citation, Disclosure, and Process Evidence:**  
  - **Consolidated under:** Anubav Vasudevan  
  - H + I will similarly be combined and may be **longer than most other sections**.

- **WS-POL-J – Students with Disabilities and Human Decision Safeguards:** Thomas Sabo  
- **WS-POL-K – Protection of Student Privacy, Data Governance, and Vendor/Procurement Governance:** Jillian Burkley  
- **WS-POL-L – Public Accountability, Notice, Consent, and Feedback:** Thomas Colvin  
- **WS-POL-M – Equity in Our Community:** Thomas Sabo  
- **WS-POL-N – School Budgeting and Workload Implications:** David Berol  
- **WS-POL-O – Reassessment and Updating of Policy:** Adriana Palacios

Each head honcho is asked to:

- **Produce an integrated draft of their section (or consolidated sections) between ½ and 2 pages in length** (longer is acceptable for the consolidated student‑use sections), written in committee voice.
- Integrate and/or summarize:
  - Existing **WS‑POL contributions**,
  - Current **section prefaces**, and
  - Any further input they choose to solicit or accept from other members.
- Use **cross‑references** (e.g., “see Section M” or “see Workstream Equity section”) where appropriate to keep the text focused and concise.

**Please email your integrated section draft(s) to me no later than _Wednesday, April 15_.**  
This will give us time to integrate everything into the master document and prepare for the extended April 24 working session.

Head honchos have full discretion to:
- Reuse or adapt existing text from contributions and prefaces,
- Solicit or accept short insertions from others,
- Cross‑reference other WS‑POL or workstream sections instead of duplicating long explanations.

---

If you need to confirm what has been said or written previously, you can use the resources in our public‑facing repository and supporting app:

- **FCCPS AI Deliverables Governance GitHub Repo**  
  - Agendas, minutes (including transcripts), workshop/survey results, workstream deliverables, prior draft contributions, and the evolving draft package.  
  - Updated daily, fully indexed, and **searchable by AI**.  
  - **URL:** https://github.com/JohnWBlack/fccps-ai-deliverables-governance

- **“Beta” FCCPS AI Deliverables and Guidance App**  
  - Reads from the same public repo.  
  - Combines workstream specs, timeline gates, and deliverable inventory status for performance KPIs and for assessing alignment on the “what” and “how” of our mission.  
  - It’s a **beta tool I built for my own assessments**, but you may find it useful.  
  - **URL:** https://governance-data-viewer.replit.app/

Thank you again for the significant time and thought you are all investing in this work. I’ll circulate the formal minutes and the next meeting invite details shortly.

Best,  
John
